messages:
gabi: Heads-up: new hire's tests failing in both Vitest and Jest. Error: 'Unexpected token export' from node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/esm/index.js.
owen: Are they importing named exports or deep-importing?
gabi: `import { createClient } from '@redwood-inference/sdk'`. Vitest with deps.inline only worked if project pkg.json has type: 'module'. Jest in CI gives ERR_REQUIRE_ESM.
leah: Typical fixes: Vitest -> deps.inline: ['@redwood-inference/sdk'] + resolve.alias to a CJS shim. Jest -> add transformIgnorePatterns: ['/node_modules/(?!@redwood-inference/sdk)'] so babel/ts-jest can compile the package. Also sometimes need NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules on CI.
owen: For jest.mock of named exports, you often need `jest.mock('@redwood-inference/sdk', () => ({ __esModule: true, createClient: jest.fn() }))` otherwise interop breaks. If module is evaluated before mock, try jest.isolateModules.
gabi: We added a local shim and pointed both runners at it; unblocks onboarding but not great. Can SDK publish a small CJS entrypoint or a test-utils mock factory?
leah: SDK-side recommendations: add a dist/cjs build, update exports map so `/utils/*` deep imports are covered, and add a `test-utils` export for mocks. We'll open an issue.
ci-bot: Created issue #437 "js-sdk: test runner compatibility (vitest/jest)" assigned @leah  https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/437
gabi: Thanks — will leave the shim until the SDK changes land. Please include a short cookbook in docs so new hires don't get blocked.
